newsitem.title: THAILAND: RESEARCH ALERT-THAI COMMS STOCKS STILL SEEN COSTLY.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-THAI COMMS STOCKS STILL SEEN COSTLY.

text.p: Most major Thai communications stocks are still expensive given doubts about the Thai economy and rising competition, analysts said on Thursday.
They said second-quarter results issued by Shinawatra Satellite Plc and Advanced Info Service Plc on Thursday were disappointing.

Shinawatra Satellite recorded a second-quarter loss of 259 million baht ($8.3 million) against a 62 million baht profit in 1996. Advanced posted a 4.7 percent rise in second-quarter profits to 928 million baht.
Advance shares were trading unchanged at 224 baht. Shinawatra Satellite's share price was down 1.75 baht to 27 in late morning trade.
Upside potential on Advance shares were limited given rises just prior to the baht's float on July 2, when the stock rose from 134 baht on June 19 to 248 on the day the baht was floated.
"Right now they are too expensive and not worth investing (in)," said Thanadech Mahapokai of Book Club Finance.

Communication stocks had lost their former lustre given the sluggish Thai economy, rising competition and steep commercial bank interest rates which had dampened consumer spending and boosted borrowing costs, Samart Rusmeerojwong of James Capel Asia said

"The business outlook of Advanced Info, especially on its profit, doesn't look good at all because of fierce competition among mobile phone operators in the country. Some of the operators have to give away incentives in order to lure people to buy their products," said Samart.
